answer.summary: Field says adding features can make tools less coherent and worse, so making Figma more powerful without making it more complicated takes constant attention. Simplicity is important to keep tools usable, but hard because complexity accumulates—even from individually sound choices—and everyone is responsible for keeping simple tasks simple while enabling complex ones.

sections.heading: Why simplification matters
sections.content: Field describes a product-building principle he calls “irreducible complexity”: adding more can make a product more complex and worse, rather than simply more capable. In tools like Figma, the challenge is to increase power without increasing complexity; if the team stops watching for complexity, the product can quickly become “a monstrosity.” He also endorses the principle, “Keep the simple things simple. Make the complex things possible.”

sections.heading: Why it is difficult
sections.content: Complexity accumulates as features are added, and even choices that work locally can combine into a system that is too complex and no longer works well. Field says teams need to revisit such systems, and that keeping things simple is everyone’s responsibility—not only leaders’.
